thread:
rajesh: Heads up — I’m seeing a weird perf cliff on FlashAttention v3 when serving causal requests with head_dim=96/128 on SM90 nodes. Latency jumps ~2.1x at seq_len ~384. Feels like an L2 spill / cache-eviction problem.
emily: hm. Did you repro with dedicated vs hosted? could be different packing/alignment in kernels.
rajesh: repro'd on dedicated SM90 and local repro on SM86 DEV box for a subset. Only reproducible when KV cache hot and long context (prefix cached) + streaming continuation. Non-causal workloads unaffected.
olga: any flamegraphs / nvprof? can you paste perf counters?
rajesh: paste from nvprof-like run (trimmed):
```
SM90 run, seq=384, head_dim=128, kernel=flash_sdpa_v3_causal
L2_hit_rate: 63% -> drops to 41% at cliff
DRAM_bw utilization +25%
shared_mem_util: steady
regs_allocated: 90
active_warps: 18/32
L2_evictions/sec: 2.4M
```
emily: that L2 hit drop is huge. v3's tiling maybe expands working set for causal KV indexing. head_dim=128 increases per-head KV stride and spills into L2.
tim: do we still fall back to v1/v2 for some shapes? selector rules should pick a different kernel if L2 pressure high.
rajesh: current selector picks v3 for >64 head_dim & causal for perf reasons — but seems to not consider cache footprint for prefix-heavy runs. selector uses seqlen threshold and head_dim only.
olga: could be interaction with KV cache layout: we append continuations and then read back large past keys, causing a high-degree-of-parallel random-access pattern across many blocks -> L2 thrash.
bench-bot: bench results attached: (simulated)
- SM80, head=64, seq=384: v2=78ms, v3=71ms
- SM90, head=128, seq=384: v3=86ms, v2=42ms  <-- regression
- SM90, head=128, seq=256: v3=39ms, v2=45ms
- SM90, head=96, seq=384: v3=92ms, v2=47ms

rajesh: so v3 only wins for certain seq ranges; but selector defaulted to v3 for head_dim>=64. That explains regression.
emily: can we make selector architecture-aware: e.g., on SM90 prefer v2 for causal when head_dim in {96,128} and seq>320? add L2-sensitive heuristic.
tim: or runtime autotune: try running microbench per model on first few requests (cheap probes) and cache the winner per model+hardware combo.
olga: autotune probe must be safe: can't delay real requests. Maybe probe in background using canary traffic or sample a small % of requests with `opt_probe=true` header.
rajesh: also need better telemetry: log kernel choice + per-request L2_miss_estimate (derived from counters) + cached_keys_size. Then we can learn thresholds automatically.
emily: short-term patch: update selector rule table: on sm90/86, causal & head_dim divisible by 32 and >=96 and seq >= 320 => pick v2. I can make PR.
rajesh: please add rollout gate: 25% traffic for 24h, compare p95 and L2_miss proxy.
olga: also add a KCACHE stress test to perf CI: create synthetic trace with long prefix reads interleaved with many small continuations.
bench-bot: suggested microbench script:
```
python -m perf.run --model tiny-llm --kernels v2,v3 --head-dims 64,96,128 --seqs 128,256,384 --device sm90
```
rajesh: I ran a quick repro script. Patch here: https://stash/redwood/patch/1234 (internal link)

emily: one more theory: v3 uses more registers to fuse steps; on SM90 the register pressure reduces occupancy such that warp scheduling causes bursts and L2 access patterns shift. Check `regs_allocated` and occupancy numbers across kernels.
rajesh: regs for v3=90, v2=56 on same shape. occupancy drop ~40%.
tim: ok plan
- emily: PR with selector table tweak + telemetry fields
- olga: add perf CI stress case
- rajesh: run 24h canary and collect counters
- tim: monitor rollout and rollback on degrade

emily: I’ll mark PR as WIP and add test vectors. will also include a fallback switch to force v2 for models that regress.
rajesh: thanks. if the autotune idea works, we can later replace static heuristics. For now let’s get the rule in and run canary.
deploy-bot: deploy started: infra/selector-config v2.3.1 -> staging (canary 25%)
olga: keeping an eye on CI jobs. will post logs if the stress test reproduces reliably.
rajesh: posting a small repro gist for anyone who wants to run locally: `gist.github.com/redwood/flash-sdpa-l2-probe` — includes nvprof commands and env vars: `FLASH_SDPA_DEBUG=1 FLASH_SELECTOR_DEBUG=1`.
tim: good thread. follow up in #eng-runtime-ops if we see production alerts.
rajesh: closing loop: will update when canary completes (ETA ~24h). :thumbsup:
